problem: Find the value of $f(x)=\frac{{e}^{⌊1-x⌋}}{x}$ at $x=-1.5.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

feedback.worked_solution:
Suppose $x$ is a real number. The greatest integer (or floor) function $⌊x⌋$ equals the greatest integer that is less than or equal to $x:$

$$
⌊x⌋=n,\,\text{where}\,n\le x<n+1,\,n\in Z.
$$

Evaluating $f(x)$ at $x=-2.5,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2.5) & =\frac{⌊(-2.5)^{3}⌋}{(-2.5)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{⌊-15.625⌋}{6.25}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, from the definition of the greatest integer function, we have

$$
⌊-15.625⌋=-16.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2.5) & =\frac{⌊-15.625⌋}{6.25} \\  & =\frac{(-16)}{6.25} \\  & =-2.56.\end{aligned}
$$
